h: Where radio was born, and other Chelmsford gems
p: Chelmsford has a proud claim to fame: it's often called the birthplace of radio, because Guglielmo Marconi opened the world's first wireless factory here in the late 1890s. You'll see nods to that heritage around the city, and Chelmsford Museum in Oaklands Park has displays on the Marconi story along with local history, natural history and a play area outside. It's a great follow-on for curious kids after a session of bouncing.

Hylands Park, on the western edge of the city, is a huge expanse of parkland with woodland walks, open lawns and the elegant Hylands House at its heart. It's a fantastic space for a picnic or a run-around. Chelmsford Cathedral in the city centre is a peaceful spot for a look around, and the riverside walks along the Chelmer and Can link up several of the city's parks.

A little further out, RHS Garden Hyde Hall near Rettendon has stunning gardens, a global growth vegetable garden and a children's play area. Danbury Country Park, to the east, has lakes, woodland and gardens to explore. A tip for AirHop: the inclusive sessions are worth knowing about if a child in your group prefers a quieter, calmer environment, and toddler sessions give younger ones the run of the place. Chelmsford has a mainline station with trains to London Liverpool Street, so it's easy to visit by train. If you're driving, the Dukes Park area is on the eastern side of the city, handy for the A12. Chelmsford's High Street and Bond Street shopping area are close by too, with plenty of places to eat once everyone's worked up an appetite.
